description: Return one Bible verse, or up to 10 verses of one chapter, word-by-word in the ORIGINAL language with lemma, Strong's number and full morphology. Use this to verify what the original text says — e.g. whether a noun is singular or plural — instead of inferring it from a translation. Pass `verse` for one verse or `verses` for several in one call. Covers the whole Bible: the OT (book 1–39) is served from the Hebrew/Aramaic Westminster Leningrad Codex; the NT (40–66) from a Greek text type chosen via `texttyp` — "byzantine" (Majority Text, default), "sblgnt" (critical), or "tr" (Textus Receptus, the only one with the Comma Johanneum). Edition and text type are labelled in the output.

texttyp.description: NT text edition: "byzantine" (Majority Text, default), "sblgnt" (critical SBL), or "tr" (Textus Receptus). Ignored for the OT (always Hebrew WLC). Compare byzantine vs. tr to see TR-only readings such as the Comma Johanneum (1Joh 5,7).

verses.description: Several verses of the chapter instead of `verse`: range "16-18" or list "1,3,5", at most 10 verses per call. Each word then carries its `vers`.

name: bible_original

kurzref.description: Same reference in the short German citation form ("2Kor 8,9.13-15"). Copy this into prose; `reference` spells the book out and is not the citation form.

verse_ohne_daten.description: Requested verses this edition does not carry. `reference` names the verses that are in the response.

vers.description: The verse this word belongs to. Present only in a multi-verse response.

wort.description: Verbatim from the edition: byzantine/tr unaccented, sblgnt accented, wlc with cantillation marks and the OSHB morpheme separator. Quote as is; do not add accents and do not smooth characters away.
